deities: Lord Lakshmi Narasimha (the nine Nava Narasimha forms: Ahobila/Ugra, Varaha/Kroda, Malola, Yogananda, Pavana, Karanja, Chatravata/Kshatravata, Bhargava, Jwala)
Ugra Sthambam (the pillar from which Narasimha emerged)
festivals: Brahmotsavam / Varshika Utsavam (Phalguna Suddha Panchami to Pournami, per veludharan.blogspot.com)

history.dynasty: Vijayanagara patronage (15th-16th century construction/expansion); later restorations
history.period: Temple structures mostly 14th-16th century; sacked by the Mughals in 1578 (radha.name), later restored
history.summary: Ahobilam is the Nava Narasimha Kshetra - nine shrines of Lord Narasimha spread across Lower Ahobilam (Diguva, the foothills village and main complex) and Upper Ahobilam (Eguva, 8 km uphill in the forest gorge), within the Nallamala/Eastern Ghats. Legend says Vishnu as Narasimha slew Hiranyakashipu here to save Prahlada, and later manifested in nine forms at Garuda's penance; 'Ahobilam' derives from the devas' cry 'Aho Balam!' ('What strength!') and also means 'great cave'. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams (sung by Thirumangai Azhvaar), the headquarters of the Ahobila Matha (founded in the late 15th century), and its main temples were built/expanded by Vijayanagara emperors, sacked by the Mughals in 1578, then restored. The Nallamala hills are personified as Adisesha: head at Tirumala, middle at Ahobilam, tail at Srisailam. CSV corrections: CSV town 'Kurnool' is WRONG - the pilgrimage town is Ahobilam itself (Allagadda mandal), ~70 km from Nandyal; CSV's district was Kurnool, but since the 2022 AP district reorganization Ahobilam falls in Nandyal district.

name: Ahobilam Temple
town_description: Ahobilam is a small pilgrim town in Allagadda mandal of Nandyal district, set in the forested Nallamala ranges of the Eastern Ghats. It exists for one reason: the Nava Narasimha temples, with Lower Ahobilam (Diguva) a roadside village temple complex and Upper Ahobilam (Eguva) 8 km into the hills via trekking trails and jeep tracks. The town has modest pilgrim lodging and eateries; the nearest sizable town is Allagadda (~24-29 km) and the district headquarters Nandyal (~68 km).

travel.railway: Nandyal railway station, approx. 68-72 km, on the Bangalore-Vizag route; taxis and buses to Allagadda then Ahobilam (per veludharan.blogspot.com and templetimings.in).
travel.road: Ahobilam is reached by road from Allagadda (24-29 km) or Nandyal (68 km); APSRTC/private buses and taxis run from Hyderabad, Kurnool, Tirupati and Chennai. Covering all nine shrines needs 1-2 days with trekking and/or jeeps; the upper-hill shrines must be visited in daylight.

visitor_information.best_time: August to December, when the forest is lush (radha.name); October to March generally, and January-February for the most comfortable trekking (templetimings.in, srivyasapooja.in). Brahmotsavam in Phalguna (Feb-March) is the grandest festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Lower (Diguva) Ahobilam: 6:30 AM-1:00 PM and 3:00 PM-8:00 PM; Upper (Eguva) Ahobilam: 7:00 AM-1:00 PM and 2:00/3:00 PM-7:00 PM (some sources cite evening close as 5:30 PM - verify locally); outlying forest shrines roughly 9:00 AM-4:00 PM. General entry ~Rs. 50 at the main temple; sevas bookable on the official Ahobilam temple website (booking.ahobilamtemple.com). Visit all shrines after sunrise and before sunset - forest safety.
